episode_title: B2B 38: How to Create Passive Income from Commissions

real_qa.q: What is the minimum investment amount to start with Secured Investment Corp's Regulation A-plus non-accredited investor fund?
real_qa.r: The Regulation A-plus fund, which opened three years ago, is open to anybody with a $1,000 minimum investment. After the initial $1,000, investors can make additional investments in $1,000 increments, up to a maximum of 10% of their annual estimated income or 10% of their estimated assets, as regulated by the SEC.
real_qa.requete: Secured Investment Corp minimum investment amount

real_qa.q: What historical returns can investors expect from Secured Investment Corp's residential real estate investment funds?
real_qa.r: The non-accredited investor fund has historically been paying out 8 to 10% annually. The funds have yielded 8 to 11% for the last eight years. Past performance is not a guarantee of future performance, but the organization maintained 10% to 11% payouts through the first year of COVID, which was maintained consistently.
real_qa.requete: Secured Investment Corp fund returns percentage

real_qa.q: How long is the lockup period for investments in Secured Investment Corp's funds, and what is the exit timeline?
real_qa.r: Investors must remain in the fund for a minimum of one year (12-month tie-up period). If divesting after that first year, the exit process takes another 12 months—investors receive 25% of their requested amount every quarter for four quarters. As stated by the fund manager: '12 months in, 12 months to get out.'
real_qa.requete: Secured Investment Corp lockup period exit timeline

real_qa.q: What are the SEC definitions of accredited versus non-accredited investors for purposes of investment fund participation?
real_qa.r: Accredited investors must meet one of two criteria: either have $1 million in assets (excluding primary residence equity) with net assets exceeding liabilities, or earn $200,000 annually as a single person or $300,000 as a married couple for the last two consecutive years. Non-accredited investors do not meet these thresholds but can access non-accredited funds with investment caps of 10% of annual income or assets.

real_qa.q: How does Secured Investment Corp's business model differ from Wall Street-dependent private lenders, particularly regarding funding stability?
real_qa.r: Secured Investment Corp does not leverage funds, rely on lines of credit, or depend on Wall Street money. Instead, it works with one-off lenders and investors who directly fund the operations. During COVID, many Wall Street-dependent lenders shut down overnight when funders demanded capital back, but Secured Investment Corp continued lending and paying 10% to 11% returns throughout the pandemic because it relied on individual investors rather than Wall Street capital.
real_qa.requete: Secured Investment Corp Wall Street funding independence

real_qa.q: What is the focus market segment for Secured Investment Corp's lending and investment activities?
real_qa.r: Secured Investment Corp focuses exclusively on the affordable housing market, specifically properties under the FHA cap (which varies by county). The company lends on and purchases single-family to four-unit properties that are non-owner occupied for investment purposes. They avoid high-end properties because they have limited buyer databases and poor returns on investment.
real_qa.requete: Secured Investment Corp affordable housing investment focus
